reusable_writing_recipes.title: Environment-split challenge list
steps: Divide challenges by environment (atmosphere vs underwater), then add operational factors like alignment and deployment.
Close with a short lessons-learned paragraph to keep the list cohesive.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Chunking by environment plus a recap prevents a long challenge list from feeling scattered.
evidence_locators: III. OWC LIMITATIONS AND CHALLENGES L232-L345

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Model matrix by impairment type
steps: List model families grouped by impairment (turbulence, pointing, AOA, noise).
Note validity regimes and tractability hints for each.
Reference any summary tables/figures if available.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Readers can quickly select models aligned to specific impairments and know their applicability.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Mitigation mini-template
steps: For each technique, give one-sentence description and target impairment.
Add a benefit sentence and a limitation/constraint sentence.
Keep each entry concise to sustain pacing.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: A fixed micro-structure keeps multiple techniques skimmable and comparable.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Research-theme triad
steps: Select three active themes (e.g., 6G alignment, ISAC, security).
For each, provide a short rationale and link back to earlier models/mitigations.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Triads keep momentum and show continuity across sections.
